[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"AWS CodeDeploy: Automated Application Deployment"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"AWS CodeDeploy is a fully managed deployment service that automates software deployments to a variety of compute services such as Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda, and your on-premises servers. CodeDeploy automates the steps required to release new software, helping you avoid error-prone manual procedures. It also allows you to quickly roll back deployments if something goes wrong."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Application: A name that uniquely identifies the application you want to deploy."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deployment Group: A set of individual instances (EC2, on-premises) targeted for deployment. Defines the deployment strategy (e.g., in-place, blue/green)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deployment Configuration: Specifies the number of instances to deploy to at a time and the success/failure conditions."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Revision: An archive containing the application code, configuration files, and AppSpec file."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"AppSpec File: A YAML or JSON file that defines the deployment actions CodeDeploy performs. It specifies the source files, destination directories, and lifecycle event hooks."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Deployment Strategies"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In-Place Deployment: Application on each instance in the deployment group is stopped, the latest version is installed, and then the new version of the application is started and validated. Downtime occurs during the deployment."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Blue/Green Deployment: New instances (the "green" environment) are provisioned with the latest application version. Traffic is then shifted from the old instances (the "blue" environment) to the new instances. This minimizes downtime and allows for easy rollback."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Lifecycle Events"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"CodeDeploy deployments proceed through a series of lifecycle events. You can specify scripts to run at each event to perform tasks such as stopping the application, installing dependencies, starting the application, and validating the deployment. Common lifecycle events include:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ApplicationStop: Used to gracefully stop the application."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BeforeInstall: Used to back up files or stop services before the installation."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install: Used to copy the application files to the destination directory."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"AfterInstall: Used to configure the application or update permissions."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ApplicationStart: Used to start the application."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ValidateService: Used to verify that the application is running correctly."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Example AppSpec File (YAML)"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"version: 0.0
os: linux
files:
  - source: /index.html
    destination: /var/www/html
hooks:
  ApplicationStop:
    - location: scripts/stop_application.sh
      timeout: 300
      runas: ec2-user
  BeforeInstall:
    - location: scripts/before_install.sh
      timeout: 300
      runas: ec2-user
  AfterInstall:
    - location: scripts/after_install.sh
      timeout: 300
      runas: ec2-user
  ApplicationStart:
    - location: scripts/start_application.sh
      timeout: 300
      runas: ec2-user
  ValidateService:
    - location: scripts/validate_service.sh
      timeout: 300
      runas: ec2-user"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Steps to Deploy an Application with CodeDeploy"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create an IAM role for CodeDeploy with the necessary permissions."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create an IAM role for the EC2 instances (or other compute resources) that allows them to be managed by CodeDeploy."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Install the CodeDeploy agent on the EC2 instances (or configure other compute resources)."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create an application in CodeDeploy."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create a deployment group, specifying the EC2 instances (or other compute resources) and the deployment configuration."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create a revision containing your application code and AppSpec file."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deploy the revision to the deployment group."},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Benefits of Using CodeDeploy"},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automated Deployments: Reduces manual effort and the risk of errors."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Faster Deployments: Speeds up the release cycle."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reduced Downtime: Blue/green deployments minimize downtime."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Centralized Control: Provides a single pane of glass for managing deployments."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rollback Capabilities: Easily revert to a previous version if a deployment fails."},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Troubleshooting Common Issues"},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CodeDeploy Agent Issues: Ensure the agent is running and properly configured on the instances. Check the agent logs for errors (usually located in /var/log/aws/codedeploy-agent/codedeploy-agent.log)."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IAM Permissions: Verify that the IAM roles have the necessary permissions for CodeDeploy to access resources and perform actions."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"AppSpec File Errors: Check the AppSpec file for syntax errors or incorrect file paths. Use a YAML validator to ensure the file is valid."},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lifecycle Event Script Failures: Review the logs for the lifecycle event scripts to identify the cause of the failure. Ensure the scripts have execute permissions and that all dependencies are installed."},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"By understanding these concepts and following the deployment steps, you can effectively use AWS CodeDeploy to automate your application deployments and improve your software release process."}]
